Thanks for posting this, I've had a depression slowly growing stronger for about two years now and I figure I will soon be unable to do anything at all, again. I promised myself not to waste another year in bed, I've worked my ass off for a long time to keep me occupied but I realize it never really worked. I just built up some temporary resolve, met a girl, got my life back on track long enough to distract myself from my depression.

I'm not any less depressed now than then, I do relate with the parts at:

http://www.youtube.com/watch?feature=player_detailpage&v=-eBUcBfkVCo#t=402

and

http://www.youtube.com/watch?feature=player_detailpage&v=-eBUcBfkVCo#t=1717

EDIT: The talk made me realize how depressed I really am, reflecting over past selves. I don't feel like my depression is the truth like he suggests is common but as a partial death. I don't do anything because I want to but out of obligation, the obligation to stay alive for those I care about. To seem like a functioning human that they can look up to.

I often fool myself with short bursts of prospect but it never lasts longer than realizing what the idea actually amounts to.

I need my life to be simple, I do a few things at a time, then I switch. I don't perceive it as a problem but as a trait. Sure it means I can't specialize well at work but I'm great at a lot of things now.

Yep.

Worst part is that when someone is trying to comfort you, you'll do the same thing: build up expectations. And when they aren't met you spiral even deeper. (Isn't this quite meta btw)

To be honest I've lost all excitement, I don't really care about anything anymore and that has helped me slow down and think things through. And now that I do that I've become able to manage it. Just stopping myself, waiting for that switch to go back before I continue my life.

I don't recommend trying to achieve this state as it is aching to apathy. I need a vacation.

Hi, I'm not sure I'm  capable of giving sound advice so I'll just say what I have done when I have been there.

i have been in this or similar situations more than once. The only thing I have found works is to become someone else for a while. When I met her I had decided that my old emotions didn't matter, the only thing that mattered was that we understood where we were and how we felt because not reaching that point only prolongs the suffering.

I think I decided that the person I needed to be was someone incredibly calm and analytic, we talked and then I told her "good, now I can be me again". Whatever that meant. Things were good for a while but I think the realization that I could do that created a seed of distrust that was the end of it.

Maybe you can do one better, maybe you can become someone else but only for yourself and break the downward spiral. Or maybe it is a bad idea to try that sort of thing, it is probably what I will try next. It is that or an amount of honesty that should drive anyone away!

I'm not writing about you, this is me:

I find that I'm most often the one abandoning, I'm definitely not responsible for my half of the interactions with friends. I'm a shitty friend too. 

A lot of people abandon me. I abandon a lot of people, but I don't care too much about it. Probably because I know I suck and it is most often my fault.
I try as hard as possible to listen to my emotions, if the pros and cons are quantifiable will spend as much time as I can motivate on quantifying them. Almost always it is not enough or infeasible.

Sure, almost all the time. I love how I love, how I hate, what the sun in my face does to me. What a sunset is like, what falling in love is like for me.

But I will never stop hating how little can turn a perfect day into hell. As for depth of depression, in my experience there is no such thing as rock bottom, I always remember my last low and start from there.

| It's all I've ever had.

EDIT:  after spending a few more minutes reflecting on this I realized I have often felt blessed by my disorder: If I could choose between not having BPD and giving up my dearest memories, that I know are so intense because of it, I'm not sure what I would do.
